answer_text:
Let

\[
f'(z)=U(x,y)+iV(x,y).
\]

We are given

\[
V(x,y)=\Im(f'(z))=6x(2y-1)=12xy-6x.
\]

Since \(f'(z)\) exists on all of \(\mathbb C\), \(f\) is entire, so \(f'\) is also entire. Therefore \(U\) and \(V\) satisfy the Cauchy-Riemann equations:

\[
U_x=V_y,\qquad U_y=-V_x.
\]

Compute

\[
V_y=12x,\qquad V_x=12y-6.
\]

Thus

\[
U_x=12x,\qquad U_y=-12y+6.
\]

Integrating \(U_x=12x\),

\[
U(x,y)=6x^2+\phi(y).
\]

Then

\[
U_y=\phi'(y)=-12y+6,
\]

so

\[
\phi(y)=-6y^2+6y+C_0,
\]

where \(C_0\) is a real constant. Hence

\[
U(x,y)=6x^2-6y^2+6y+C_0.
\]

Therefore

\[
f'(z)=6x^2-6y^2+6y+i(12xy-6x)+C_0.
\]

Recognize that

\[
6x^2-6y^2+i12xy=6z^2
\]

and

\[
6y-6ix=-6iz.
\]

So

\[
f'(z)=6z^2-6iz+C_0,
\]

where \(C_0\in\mathbb R\).

Integrating,

\[
f(z)=2z^3-3iz^2+C_0z+C_1.
\]

Use \(f(0)=3-2i\):

\[
C_1=3-2i.
\]

Use \(f(1)=5-5i\):

\[
f(1)=2-3i+C_0+3-2i=5-5i+C_0.
\]

Since \(f(1)=5-5i\), we get \(C_0=0\). Thus

\[
f(z)=2z^3-3iz^2+3-2i.
\]

Now evaluate at \(z=1+i\). Since

\[
(1+i)^2=2i,\qquad (1+i)^3=-2+2i,
\]

we have

\[
\begin{aligned}
f(1+i)
&=2(-2+2i)-3i(2i)+3-2i\\
&=-4+4i+6+3-2i\\
&=5+2i.
\end{aligned}
\]

\[
\boxed{5+2i}
\]
